answer: The node's own SSHv2 host keys are shown with 'show ssh-host-key-<public-key-algorithm> [public-key] [label] [fingerprint-algorithm] [fingerprint]'. These are the global host keys used by both server-side and client-side SSHv2 based apps. There must be one host key per supported algorithm, so yes, there can be more than one. The system auto-generates a host-key in the default DB, and additional host-keys can be added or overwritten via the ssh-keygen RPC. Supported public-key-algorithm values are ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ssh-rsa2048, ssh-rsa3072, ssh-rsa4096 and ssh-ed25519 (ED25519 support starts at R9.0). public-key is a PEM-encoded string 0..2048 chars, label 0..256 chars, fingerprint-algorithm is md5 or sha256 and fingerprint is 0..95 chars. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: 'show ssh-host-key-ecdsa-sha2-nistp521'.

ssh-keygen generates an SSH private/public key pair and the existing keys in the system are replaced by the newly generated pair. Syntax: 'ssh-keygen [-b=<key-length>] [-l=<key-label>] [-t=<type>]', Operational mode only. -t selects rsa, ecdsa or ed25519; the default type is rsa. -b selects strength: with secure mode (security-policies/secure-mode) disabled, RSA supports 2048, 3072 or 4096 (default 2048) and ECDSA supports 256, 384 or 521 (default 256); with secure mode enabled, RSA supports only 4096 and ECDSA supports 384 or 521 (default 384). ED25519 is 256 regardless of secure mode. -l sets the key label; if omitted the label is the value of ne-id. Retrieve the new public key with 'show ssh-host-key'.

Pre-trust a peer by creating an SSHv2 known-hosts entry: 'add ssh-known-host-<id> address <value> public-key-algorithm <value> public-key <value> [label <value>]'. id is a unique name, string 0..64 chars. address is the hostname, IPv4 or IPv6 address of the allowed/known peer host (an IPv4 or IPv6 address may carry a zone index after a % sign; otherwise the device default zone is used). public-key-algorithm must be one of ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ssh-rsa2048, ssh-rsa3072, ssh-rsa4096 or ssh-ed25519 (ED25519 from R9.0). public-key is the OpenSSH public key in PEM format, 0..2048 chars; label is 0..256 chars. Use 'set ssh-known-host-<id> [label <value>]' to change the label, 'show ssh-known-host-<id>' to display, and 'delete ssh-known-host-<id>' to remove. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

The trusted-certificate object holds the X509v3 CA (Root and Intermediate) certificates trusted by the system. Use 'show trusted-certificate[-id] ...' to view attributes such as version (v3), serial-number, subject-name, issuer, trust-chain, valid-from, valid-to, modification-time, status (in-use, unused, revoked, expired, available, pending-import, invalid, untrusted, future, valid, unsupported), public-key-length (rsa2048/rsa3072/rsa4096/ecdsa256/ecdsa384/ecdsa521), public-key-type (rsa, ecdsa), signature-key-type (rsa, ecdsa, rsassa-pss), signature-hash-algorithm (sha256, sha384, sha512, sha1), certificate-bytes, key-usage and extended-key-usage. Settable attributes are revocation-mode (auto, force-revoked, force-unrevoked; default auto), alarm-report-control (allowed, inhibited; default allowed) and label. To remove a certificate use the clear command (clear certificate).

Issue 'terminate cable-id' in Operational mode to stop all running CableID verification tests. Because CableID verification runs on a port-pair basis, the test can only be stopped after the current port-pair verification completes and before the next port-pair starts: the in-flight port-pair runs to completion, so the maximum delay to terminate is one port-pair verification time. The test is known to be terminated once the cable-id-status cable-id-state changes to idle; after issuing the command use 'show cable-id cable-id-status' to confirm the cable-id entity is back in the idle state. The 'show cable-id' / 'terminate cable-id' pair is documented under the cable-id entity; show is also available in Candidate Configuration mode, terminate only in Operational mode.

The CableID signal can only be sourced or terminated by the CAD10A and RD20TM cards; the signal is passed transparently through the OPSM. A CableID path starts at the end A port and terminates at the end Z port where the signal is sourced/terminated, that is at a CAD10A DWDM port or an RD20TM ADE port. Accordingly, cable-id-path card-type-a and card-type-z can only take the values RD20TM or CAD10A, and port-a/port-z are port AIDs on a CableID-capable sled. The card type value is derived from the provisioned fiber-connection at that port: when a fiber-connection is created, the CableID function checks whether it terminates on a port of a CableID-capable sled and, if so, records that card type into the CableID path topology as card-type-a or card-type-z. View with 'show cable-id-path-<name>'.

Yes. The cable-id-status container holds the process status and progress of a CableID-based fiber connection verification, and you may issue 'show cable-id cable-id-status' at any time to query progress. Syntax: 'show cable-id-status [cable-id-state] [test-progress]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. cable-id-state is idle (verification not running), running-incl-switching (running for both active and protected paths) or running-no-switching (running for the active path only); default idle. test-progress is a string 0..255 chars, default 'None', showing 'Not applicable' if cable-id-state is disabled, otherwise 'N out of M completed' where M is the total number of port-pairs to be tested and N the number already completed, for example '1 out of 1 completed.'

Each carrier can discover up to one node. carrier-neighbor shows the local carrier instance that has discovered a neighbor node, and it is possible for multiple collocated carriers to discover the same node multiple times, each time connected to a different remote carrier. Syntax: 'show carrier-neighbor-<local-carrier> [last-update] [age] [local-carrier-id] [ne-id] [ne-name] [ne-type] [remote-carrier-id] [ipv4-loopback-address] [ipv6-loopback-address]', in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. local-carrier is a string 0..16 chars; ne-id and ne-name are 0..256 chars; ne-type is 0..64 chars; remote-carrier-id is the AID of the remote carrier (0..64 chars) and implies a specific remote port id. The loopback addresses may be empty if not configured.

Use 'show connection-ports-<degree-number>/<index> [port-name]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. degree-number is a uint16 in range 1..20 and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. index is a uint32 in range 1..2 and is always 1 in the 1830 GX, since dwdm-line ports are bi-directional. port-name is the dwdm-line port of an RD or ILAx card, and as a consequence the OMS of the corresponding dwdm-port is created. 'show connection-ports*' lists all connection ports in the node, giving output such as connection-ports-1/1 -> port-1-3-dwdm-line1; 'show connection-ports-5/1' shows the single entry, for example port-name port-4-1-dwdm-line1.

custom-tlv shows the list of Organizational Specific TLV (Type-Length-Value) parameters. Syntax: 'show custom-tlv-<lldp-port>/<direction>/<oui>/<subtype> [value]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. lldp-port is the local port associated with the LLDP agent, string 0..64 chars. direction is the direction associated with the LLDP statistics, either ingress or egress. oui is the Organization Unique Identifier of the TLV, a hexadecimal representation of the 24-bit identifier, string 1..6 chars. subtype is the sub-type identifier of the TLV within the scope of that OUI, string 1..507 chars. The value attribute carries the TLV content.

No. The external-fiber-connection is set autonomously by TNMS; although it is possible to configure it manually, it is not recommended to do so. external-fiber-connection represents the physical link between two ports of L0 cards in different NEs, or in the same NE in disaggregated configurations. Syntax: 'add external-fiber-connection-<name> src-port-name <value> dst-port-name <value> [label] [scope] [src-node-id] [src-card-name] [dst-node-id] [dst-card-name] [fiber-connection-type]', plus set (label only), show and delete. name is 0..64 chars, node-ids 0..256, card names 0..64, port names 0..128. fiber-connection-type is one-way or two-way, default two-way. scope is general-purpose (default) or cable-id; if scope is not cable-id, CableID verification excludes that connection from the CableID path.

fiber-connection is the physical link representation of a connection between two distinct ports (or two distinct sub-ports) in the same NE, used in an OADM/ILA topology: 'add|set fiber-connection-<name> [label] [src-port] [dst-port] [fiber-connection-type]', with show and delete. external-fiber-connection is the physical link representation of a connection between two ports of L0 cards in different NEs, or in the same NE in disaggregated configurations, and it carries additional attributes: scope (general-purpose or cable-id, default general-purpose), src-node-id, src-card-name, src-port-name, dst-node-id, dst-card-name and dst-port-name. The external one is set autonomously by TNMS and manual configuration is not recommended. Both have fiber-connection-type one-way or two-way, default two-way, name 0..64 chars, label 0..256 chars, no pre- or post-conditions.

Yes. icdp is the Nokia Carrier Discovery Protocol (ICDP, Intelligent Carrier Discovery Protocol) and its global-switch flag defaults to true, so it is enabled by default. Syntax: 'set icdp global-switch <true|false>' and 'show icdp [global-switch]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The global-switch is the flag that enables icdp; permitted values are true and false. The icdp object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Example: 'set icdp global-switch true'. The neighbors that ICDP finds are viewed through carrier-neighbor, where each carrier can discover up to one node.

INCI is the Inter-NE Communication Interface/Infrastructure. It provides API-based communication infrastructure for control plane communication across different network elements, for example a transponder such as CHM6 on 1830 GX G40 and a line system such as FLEXILS. INCI uses a gRPC server/client as the core mechanism: when the INCI service is enabled the gRPC server starts and binds to the local IP address, and when an INCI neighbor instance is configured gRPC client sessions are established. It is not running by default: 'set inci [inci-enabled <true|false>]' and 'show inci [inci-enabled]', with inci-enabled taking true or false and defaulting to false. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Enable with 'set inci inci-enabled true'.

Compare configured-node-name with discovered-node-name on the inci-neighbor. configured-node-name is the user-provisioned name of the remote NE and is explicitly used to compare against the discovered-node-name, which is the name of the remote NE as sent by the remote NE; both are strings 0..128 chars. discovered-node-id (string 0..12) carries the node ID received from the remote node. Use 'show inci-neighbor-<neighbor-id> [neighbor-address] [neighbor-port] [connection-status] [configured-node-name] [discovered-node-name] [discovered-node-id] [alarm-report-control] [oper-state]'. neighbor-id is the node-ID AID of the provisioned neighbor; oper-state is enabled or disabled; alarm-report-control is allowed or inhibited, default inhibited. configured-node-name and neighbor-address are mandatory on add.

Two timers on interface-neighbor control this. discovery-cycle-time is the periodicity at which SNDP discover messages are sent, range 30..300 seconds, default 30. discovery-timeout is the time after which discovery is considered failed; when this timeout occurs the neighbor-adjacency-state transitions to blackout. Its range is 300..1800 seconds, default 300. Set them with 'set interface-neighbor-<local-interface> [discovery-cycle-time <value>] [discovery-timeout <value>] [discovery-enabled <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [label <value>]'. discovery-enabled is true or false, default true, and switches discovery on the local interface. neighbor-adjacency-state can be blackout, discovery, holding or unknown, default unknown. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

No. The links container within the topology is dynamically filled in by the system, allowing the NCT topology to be derived and displayed. The command is simply 'show links', with no command parameters, available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The same applies to nct-connection, which shows the existing links between NCT ports in a multi-chassis NE and is likewise dynamically filled in by the system.

The global lldp object carries the hold-on-timer, which is the time to keep neighbor information in the case where the neighbor does not supply an explicit Time-To-Live (TTL) TLV. It is a number of seconds and its default is 900. Use 'show lldp [hold-on-timer]' to view the global LLDP configuration and 'set lldp [hold-on-timer <value>]' to change it, for example 'set lldp hold-on-timer 60'. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, and the lldp object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. On lldp-neighbor, the per-neighbor ttl attribute gives the seconds until the remote system information expires, and if the remote system does not provide a ttl value that parameter is set to the global hold-on-timer.

'show lldp-local-info-<lldp-port> [chassis-id-subtype] [chassis-id] [port-id-subtype] [port-id] [port-description] [system-name] [system-description] [supported-capabilities] [enabled-capabilities]' shows the LLDP local system information sent on an LLDP port. The 1830 GX NE advertises chassis-id-subtype chassis-component with the chassis serial number as chassis-id; port-id-subtype local with the port AID as port-id; port-description set to the port name; system-name set to the NE name; and system-description set to the string 'Nokia Corporation.Converged OS, Version <release id> build <software label>'. All these strings are 0..255 chars. supported-capabilities and enabled-capabilities are router and bridge. Example: 'show lldp-local-info-comm-eth-1-11-ETH4'.

No. For lldp-neighbor the egress direction is not supported: the direction key is the direction in which the neighbor was detected and its only value is ingress. Syntax: 'show lldp-neighbor-<lldp-port>/<direction> [last-update] [age] [chassis-id-subtype] [chassis-id] [port-id-subtype] [port-id] [port-description] [system-name] [system-description] [supported-capabilities] [enabled-capabilities] [ttl]', in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The same restriction applies to lldp-port-statistics, where direction is ingress only. Example: 'show -r lldp-neighbor-ethernet-1-1-3/ingress'. The neighbor information is kept indefinitely until the port is decommissioned or the data is manually cleared by the user.

No. All counter values in an lldp-port-statistics entry are maintained on a continuing basis and are not deleted upon expiration of the TTL timing counters associated with the LLDP neighbor information. The counters do freeze: all statistical counters associated with a particular port on the local LLDP agent become frozen whenever lldp-admin-status is disabled for that port. Syntax: 'show lldp-port-statistics-<lldp-port>/<direction> [last-change-time] [last-clear-time] [total-ageouts] [total-discarded-frames] [error-frames] [total-frames-in] [total-frames-out] [total-discarded-tlvs] [total-unrecognized-tlvs]'; direction is ingress only, egress is not supported. Counters default to 0, last-clear-time defaults to 0000-01-01T00:00:00Z, and total-ageout counts the times a neighbor was deleted from the lldp-neighbor list due to TTL expiry.

Use 'show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port> [src-chassis] [dst-chassis] [src-chassis-state] [dst-chassis-state]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. It shows NCT connectivity information, that is the existing links between NCT ports in a multi-chassis NE, dynamically filled in by the system so the NCT topology can be derived. src-chassis-state and dst-chassis-state take the values node controller, provisioned or unprovisioned. src-chassis and dst-chassis are the chassis AID if commissioned, or the chassis serial number if unprovisioned (strings 0..64). Likewise src-port and dst-port must be NCT ports: the port AID for a commissioned chassis, or the format '<chassis-serial-number>-<slot>-NCT-<id>' for an unprovisioned chassis.

The sndp command sets or shows the SNDP (Simple Neighbor Discovery Protocol) feature switch. Syntax: 'set sndp [sndp-enabled <value>]' and 'show sndp [sndp-enabled]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. sndp-enabled is the single attribute, a switch controlling the sndp feature, with values true or false and default true, so SNDP is on unless disabled. Example: 'show sndp sndp-enabled'. SNDP discover messages are the ones sent on management interfaces per the interface-neighbor discovery-cycle-time (30..300 seconds, default 30), with per-interface control through interface-neighbor discovery-enabled.

'add submarine-link-<name> src-node-id <value> src-port-name <value> dst-node-id <value> dst-port-name <value> degree-target-tx-power <value> [...]' with set, show and delete. The mandatory attributes are src-node-id and dst-node-id (the NE names of the source and destination nodes, 0..256 chars), src-port-name and dst-port-name (the OTS dwdm-line port of the degree, 0..128 chars), and degree-target-tx-power, the launch power at the ROADM into the primary fiber. fiber-length defines the fiber length in km of the associated fiber pair, a decimal64 in range 0..25000 km with default 0, and it excludes the length of branch segments. Other attributes: fiber-connection-type two-way (default) or one-way, link-name, fiber-pair-id, segment-list (0..512), bu-segment-index (uint16, default 0, 0 for end nodes), rx/tx-fiber-type, gsnr, degree-expected-rx-power, commissioning-snr-margin, launch-condition flat-tx or pfib (default pfib), and allocated-spectrum-list of start/end frequency pairs, max 32 elements.

supporting-fiber-connection shows the list of fiber connections supporting a path. Syntax: 'show supporting-fiber-connection-<name> [fiber-connection-list]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. name is the name of the entity, string 0..64 chars, and fiber-connection-list is the supported fiber connection path, an instance-identifier. The same container appears under cable-id-path: it is displayed when the -r flag is used with 'show -r cable-id-path-<name>', which for a single port shows the results from the port-pair including all cable-id-path parameters plus the supporting fiber connections, for example 'supporting-fiber-connection-1-6-ade6-1-8-ade6' with fiber-connection-list 'supporting-fiber-connection-R1'.
